items.title: A flat separated morphism injective on generic points is universally injective
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a morphism f : X -> Y that is flat and separated, with trivial residue field extensions at the generic points of X and injective on those generic points, the lemma concludes that f is universally injective (statement lines 6675-6684). The proof reduces universal injectivity to surjectivity of the diagonal, argues by contradiction: if Delta misses a point then its image being closed lets one pick a generic point eta of a component of X x_Y X outside the image; the first projection is flat as a base change of f, so generalisations lift and the preimage xi of eta is a generic point of X; but the assumptions force the fibre (X x_Y X)_{f(xi)} to have at most one point, contradicting Delta(xi) = eta (proof lines 6687-6702). The level is H3: a genuine point-theoretic argument using flatness through the lifting of generalisations, with every step named.
